source.title: Grokking at the Edge of Linear Separability
source.authors: A. Beck; N. Levi; Yohai Bar-Sinai

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures training-time generalization dynamics in logistic classification and reports non-monotonic test loss and delayed generalization, bearing on V2. It does not reproduce a model-size double-descent experiment.
record.gate_note: The relevant findings are the study's own training-time test-loss and test-accuracy results. Double descent is mentioned only as related literature; cited results are not included. The paper does not sweep model size at fixed training data or isolate increasing sample size near an interpolation threshold.
record.test_reason: This is a grokking study of linear logistic classification with all-identical labels. It tracks test loss and accuracy over training near the d/N = 1/2 separability threshold. It measures delayed generalization, not double descent. No curve shows test error falling, rising and then falling over model size, epochs or samples. The only mention of double descent is a sentence in the discussion linking it to criticality (citing Schaeffer et al.). The reader's V2 link treats grokking's non-monotonic test loss as epoch-wise double descent, but the paper never measures or claims that. The model is also linear, not a deep network.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that grokking arises in logistic classification near the critical point lambda = 1/2, where data becomes linearly separable from the origin, through critical slowing down along flat directions. They conjecture that grokking generally occurs near interpolation thresholds and only mention that double descent has been proposed to relate to criticality; they do not test double descent.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses linear logistic classification and analyzes grokking near a separability threshold; it does not use the original double-descent model-size, epoch, or sample-size sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported time dynamics vary with lambda, feature-noise scale, optimizer, loss choice, initial conditions, data distribution, and label fraction.

fits_no_version.finding: In linear logistic classification with identical labels, grokking (delayed generalization with non-monotonic test loss) appears only when d/N approaches 1/2 from below. The authors call 1/2 the effective interpolation threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking and critical slowing down occur near interpolation or separability thresholds.

fits_no_version.finding: Across a lambda sweep (Fig. 1 right), final accuracy is perfect below lambda = 1/2 and imperfect above it, falling with the margin. Grokking time and the norm of S diverge at 1/2. There is no second descent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Asymptotic generalization changes non-analytically at the separability threshold in linear logistic regression.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning; PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The evidence concerns a specific linear binary-classification setup rather than deep networks. Most relevant curves are plotted without numerical values or uncertainty estimates, and the analytic results use the gradient-flow limit while experiments use finite learning rates.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported training-time generalization findings were intentionally omitted. Supplemental plots are recorded as figure-only where the text gives no numeric values.

untested.parts: All; the model is linear and there is no deep-network size sweep.
All; the paper tracks grokking dynamics, not a fall-rise-fall test-error curve over epochs.
All; the lambda sweep shows no second descent past the threshold.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's tests/T2 classification for V2 conflates grokking's non-monotonic test loss with epoch-wise double descent. I reclassified the study as discussing the claim (T6) and set every row to versions none. The Fig. 1 right-panel lambda sweep is a capacity-like sweep through a threshold but shows no second descent, and the setup has no feature signal.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or test-error peak near the size that just fits the training set.
The study reports non-monotonic test loss and delayed test-accuracy improvement, not a tabulated test-classification-error curve or a direct comparison with a model-wise curve.
No experiment increases training sample count near an interpolation threshold while holding the other relevant settings fixed.
No capacity sweep establishes a general double-descent curve across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location across size, epochs, and sample count.

The study varies feature noise and optimizers in grokking experiments, but does not test whether a double-descent peak is caused by label noise or variance, splits into multiple peaks, or disappears under optimally tuned regularization.
No re-counting of parameters by effective number is tested against a double-descent curve.

reader_labels.reason: The authors report non-monotonic test loss and delayed generalization in these training-time settings (R1-R3, R6, R8, R10-R12, R15-R21).
